summary:
I checked all six claimed causes against the code and with my own scratch scripts. Four hold as stated. Two need corrections, and I found one cause the investigator missed. The galaxy draws on the shared world runtime (src/runtime/*). It enters through rt.mount after a fixed 1250 ms timer started at the click (Universe.jsx:205). The jump overlay keeps its own wall clock and never waits for the galaxy.

Visible discontinuities on entry, most likely first:
(a) The hand-off. The overlay clears or is cut off before the galaxy draws. Then you get the dark 'Plotting a course' page, and the scene pops in with no fade. In light mode a white wash can also appear, because the new page fades in from opacity 0 over the light body. I reproduced this in a production build (vite build into the scratchpad, then vite preview). The page swap committed while the overlay was at most ~79% opaque. A 2.9 s main-thread task right after the commit kept the page-in fade from starting. The overlay was removed having skipped its tunnel and exit, with the page at opacity 0.13 over the white body. So the white wash is not dev-only, though headless SwiftShader makes the stalls much longer than a real GPU would.
(b) One blank frame, plus a jump in sharpness and star size, whenever the quality governor changes level. The runtime resizes the drawing buffer after the frame's draw. I confirmed this with a minimal WebGL page: draw then resize in the same rAF shows the page background; resize then draw is fine.
The pixel-ratio fight is real, and I measured it: at DPR 2 the galaxy draws at 2.0, not its 1.5 cap (gfx.ratio says 1.5). At DPR 1 it draws at 1.25 (gfx.ratio says 1). At DPR 1.5 there is no fight. So the first governor step is a 59% pixel cut in one frame.

Corrections to the investigator:
- The transparent frame logged at place() is an artifact of their detector. place() runs in a setTimeout-driven task, and the next rAF draws before the browser paints.
- The resize and adopt triggers don't fire on entry. The host never changes size, and adopt's blank sits under an opaque snapshot cover. On entry only quality changes trigger the blank frame.
- The dev StrictMode double backend is worse than stated. Whichever backend resolves last wins, so in 1 of 3 runs the surviving gfx never got the module's ratio (gfx.ratio 1, drawing at 2.0, post samples 0).
- Fix 5 as written would break the governor. quality.reset() does not reset the pace's level, so the next step jumps from level 0 straight to 4.
- Fix 3 removes the resize that currently wipes a re-attached canvas. A re-attached WebGL canvas shows its last frame until it is drawn again, so fix 7's fade is needed alongside it.

Missed cause: the 1250 ms navigation timer runs from the click, not from the overlay's start. When the overlay starts late, the page swap shows through it while it is still semi-transparent.

Unrelated latent bug found on the way: rt's `shown` flag carries over from one world to the next. If the previous world's box was scrolled out of view, the galaxy never draws and stays on 'Plotting a course' (reproduced in Node).

rootCauses.title: A drawing-buffer resize after the frame's draw shows one blank frame. On entry, quality-level changes are the trigger.
rootCauses.mechanism: runtime.js frame() draws (84-86), then calls quality.frame(t). On a level change it calls gfx.setRatio (99-103), which writes the canvas size (gfx.js:32-36) after the draw in the same task. With preserveDrawingBuffer off (renderer.js:39) and clear alpha 0 (renderer.js:49), the compositor shows the cleared, transparent buffer: one frame of the dark page background, with the planet and stars gone. Correction to the investigator: rt.resize and rt.adopt are not entry triggers. The galaxy host is inset:0 of a 100svh page and never changes size during entry. The ResizeObserver's first callback arrives while the module is still loading and is ignored (useWorld.js:68-71). adopt's resize (runtime.js:396-397) happens under the opaque snapshot cover. Window resizes still blank, because RO callbacks run after rAF, but those are user-driven.
rootCauses.evidence: reattach.mjs, a minimal WebGL2 canvas with alpha and no preserveDrawingBuffer: draw red, then width 200→100 in the same rAF → screenshot rgb 0,0,255 (page background); resize then draw → 255,0,0; same-size write (200→200) → still red. rtsim.mjs, the real runtime with fakes: frame order 'draw → setRatio 1.5 → lowerQuality 1'. The WebGL spec presents the drawing buffer at the next composite after a canvas resize. The investigator's run3 BLANK and screencast #45 used a synthetic governor clock, so they show the mechanism, not how often it happens.

rootCauses.title: Pixel-ratio fight: createRenderer's fit() overrides the runtime's ratio, so at DPR 2 the galaxy draws at 2.0, not its 1.5 cap
rootCauses.mechanism: webgl.js:58-62 routes gfx.setSize through gl.setSize, which runs fit() (renderer.js:56-59, 87-91). fit() re-applies createRenderer's private pixelRatio = pixelRatio(budget.ratio) (renderer.js:51; device.js:184-188): 2 at DPR 2, and max(dpr, 1.25) on the high tier. gfx.setRatio (gfx.js:32-36) never updates that value. So place() (runtime.js:230) and every rt.resize go back to 2.0 (1.25 at DPR 1), and each quality change goes to ratioUnder(1.5) × scale. The first step at DPR 2 is 2.0 → 1.275, a 59% pixel cut, and coming back up gives 1.5, not 2.0. Stars, beacons, dust and world uniforms are sized for gfx.ratio (scene.js:1755-1759, 1881, 2197, 2231; sky.js:186, 212, 503-506). They draw 25% small at 2.0 and jump to full size at the first step, a visible star-size change on top of the blank frame. post.js:217 picks 4 MSAA samples at create time (renderer at 1.5 then, 2 when `small`) but draws at 2.0. That is the costly case its own comment (213-216) warns about, which makes governor steps more likely.
rootCauses.evidence: ratio.mjs / ratio2.mjs (headless, ?quality=high, 400x240 box). DPR 2: gfxRatio 1.5, renderer 2, buffer 800x480. After setRatio(ratioFor): 1.5, 630x375. After a window resize back: renderer 2 again, 800x480. DPR 1: gfxRatio 1, renderer 1.25. DPR 1.5: 1.5 and 1.5 (no fight). Consistent with the investigator's run2/run3.

rootCauses.title: The quality governor can step on arrival hitches, bounce, and floor even when frames have recovered
rootCauses.mechanism: pace.js steps down when ≥25% of a 20-frame run is late (77, 90-104), at least 600 ms apart, and steps up after 4 s clean, doubling the wait after a bounce (101, 111-116). Arrival work (model GLBs uploading and linking via models.want/warm, war-front ships, the React HUD mounting when status flips to 'on', and in dev synchronous shader-error checks at renderer.js:44) can produce such runs. Each step is one blank frame (cause 1) plus a sharpness and star-size change (cause 2). quality.js:61-69 floors 2.5 s after reaching the last step without checking that frames are still late, unlike its header (3-6). quality.reset() has no production callers, so state carries across worlds. Also found: quality.reset() would not reset the pace's level (pace.js:48-53), so it can't simply be called per world.
rootCauses.evidence: Re-ran the investigator's pace-sim2.mjs on the real modules with my extension-resolving loader. E (60 Hz, 6 hitches in the first second): 0.7 s→L1 (1.275), 5.2 s→L0 (1.5). I (1 in 4 frames over the beat): L1-L4 in 2.9 s, floored at 5.4 s. F (120 Hz) and G (3 hitches): 0 changes. resetsim.mjs: after three steps, reset() gives quality.level 0 but pace.level 3, and the next late run jumps 0→4. With clean frames it 'improves' from 0 to 2. Not observed on real hardware: headless runs at 2-3 fps, and gaps over 250 ms are ignored (pace.js:68).

rootCauses.title: Hand-off: the overlay ends on its own clock, so it clears onto the loading page, or is cut off mid-tunnel, and the page-in fade can wash white
rootCauses.mechanism: The overlay's clock is wall time from its first frame (Hyperspace.jsx:183-186; hyperspace3d/scene.js:308-311) and ends at T.end=2450 ms (Hyperspace.jsx:256-260; scene.js:334-340). Nothing holds it for the galaxy: holdJump is used only for in-galaxy jumps (Galaxy.jsx:276-281). The Galaxy chunk is not prefetched (App.jsx:31, 298-311). HashRouter navigates inside startTransition (react-router 7.18.4, chunk-OB3PAWPO.mjs:10545-10551), so the universe page stays up until the chunk is in. The galaxy page then mounts inside .page-enter (App.jsx:325), which fades from opacity 0 over 0.2 s (index.css:834-835) on top of body var(--bg) #fdfdfc in light mode. That fade only starts on the first paint after the commit, so a main-thread stall right after the commit pushes the whole wash past the overlay's end. A starved overlay's next frame lands past T.end and it removes itself without the tunnel and clear-out. GalaxyIntro is portaled, fixed and black (galaxy.css:406-413), so it masks the first entry of each session.
rootCauses.evidence: prodentry.mjs on a production build: click 0; overlay canvas +2521; galaxy page committed +2865 (page opacity 0.00 at +2915); 2927 ms long task from +2943; overlay removed +5902 with page opacity 0.13 and no overlay; first world draw +8558. Dev evidence from the investigator: run2 #6 94.9% near-white, run4 with a 4 s delay shows the universe page again before the galaxy. Headless SwiftShader exaggerates the stalls. On a real GPU, how often the white wash appears depends on how long the post-commit work takes (the runtime's WebGL context, the 303 KB scene chunk, scene.create). The overlay clearing before the first draw (READY_WAIT up to 4 s) is near-certain on a first entry.

rootCauses.title: Missed: the page swap is timed from the click, not from the overlay, so when the overlay starts late the swap shows through it
rootCauses.mechanism: go() navigates after a fixed 1250 ms from the click (Universe.jsx:205; flight.js:130), meant to land on the flash. The overlay's t=0 is its first drawn frame, after the lazy chunk, jumpScene and an async precompile (hyperspace3d/scene.js:343-345). darkAt is below 1 until t=450 ms (timeline.js:29). If the overlay starts more than ~800 ms after the click, the universe → galaxy swap (including the light body under the opacity-0 page) happens while the overlay is still partly transparent. App never passes onPeak (App.jsx:116-120).
rootCauses.evidence: prodentry.mjs: a 2167 ms long task at +354 after the click; overlay canvas appended at +2521, first frame later still; galaxy page committed at +2865. The overlay was at most ~344 ms into its timeline (darkAt ≤ ease(0.76)·0.92 ≈ 0.79), so the swap showed through it. The size of that first stall is likely a SwiftShader artifact (WebGL context and renderer creation for the overlay). The decoupling itself is in the code.

rootCauses.title: The world canvas pops in after a dark loading gap with no fade. The investigator's transparent place() frame is not real.
rootCauses.mechanism: .world-canvas has no fade (runtime.css), unlike .scene-canvas (index.css:904-905). The page shows 'Plotting a course…' (GalaxyView.jsx:114-118) until the first frame sets status 'on' (runtime.js:104), then the scene appears all at once in its 'exit' arrival (scene.js:1780). Correction: place() runs in a task resolved from setTimeout-driven precompile polling (renderer.js:404-417, settle). The next rendering update runs the rAF draw before it paints, so no transparent frame is presented. The investigator's BLANK at place() comes from checking at the next rAF's start, before that rAF's draw. Related hazard: a re-attached WebGL canvas shows its last frame until drawn. Today the ratio fight's resize at place() usually clears it, but not at DPR 1.5. It would become visible after fix 3 if the first draw is ever delayed.
rootCauses.evidence: prodentry.mjs: 'Plotting a course' shown +2865 → first world draw +8558 → text removed +8579. reattach.mjs case 3/4: detached 200 ms, re-attached at the same size, no draw → screenshot still red (stale frame shown).

rootCauses.title: Dev only: the StrictMode double mount makes two WebGL backends and leaks one; nondeterministically the survivor never gets the module's ratio
rootCauses.mechanism: Both rt.mount calls reach backendFor while gfx is null (runtime.js:180-191). Whichever makeBackend resolves last becomes gfx, regardless of mount order, and the other is never disposed. build's gfx.setRatio (runtime.js:197) can land on the losing backend. The scene is then created on a renderer still at createRenderer's 2.0: gfx.ratio 1, so stars and dust are sized for 1 while drawing at 2.0, and post samples are 0. Dev's checkShaderErrors (renderer.js:44) also lengthens hitches, so the governor (cause 3) steps more in dev than in production.
rootCauses.evidence: rtsim.mjs: two concurrent mounts → 'backends made: 2', rt.gfx is #2, no dispose of #1. ratio2.mjs at DPR 2, three runs: contexts #1/#2 created 25 ms apart and mount1 resolved false afterwards → final gfxRatio 1, renderer 2, samples 0. The other two runs: gfxRatio 1.5, renderer 2, samples 2.

proposals.title: Apply the quality level before the draw
proposals.description: In src/runtime/runtime.js frame(), move `const level = quality.frame(t); if (level !== null) { gfx.setRatio(ratioFor(current.module)); world.lowerQuality?.(level); }` (99-103) inside the try, above input.sample/world.step/world.draw (84-86). Keep the snapshot block (92-98) after the draw: the cover must be read in the frame's own task (runtime.js:152-167). Every ratio change is then followed by a draw in the same task, so no blank frame (reattach.mjs case 6). This is correct and complete for blank frames from quality changes in every runtime world. It does not remove the sharpness change; proposals 3 and 5 address that.
proposals.tests: runtime.test.js: gfx.setRatio, world.lowerQuality and world.draw push into one order array; quality.frame returns 1 on a tick → ['setRatio','lowerQuality','draw']. The existing 'a new quality level sets the ratio and tells the world' and module-cap tests (317-337) still pass. A frame whose draw throws after a level change still fails the world.

proposals.title: Hold the jump until the galaxy draws, navigate on the overlay's dark, prefetch, and drop the light page-in under world pages
proposals.description: (1) Universe.jsx go(): when `to` starts with '/galaxy' and plan.mode is 'jump', take a hold before navigating, for example a module-level `pendingHold = holdJump(8000)` exported from timeline.js. Release it the first time the galaxy's status is 'on', 'failed' or 'lost', when GalaxyView mounts with meant false (3D off, or WorldGate holding), and when GalaxyView unmounts. A useEffect on useWorld's status in GalaxyView is enough. Hyperspace2D (Hyperspace.jsx:185), the 3D overlay (hyperspace3d/scene.js:310) and the crews' JumpCanvas (jumps/JumpCanvas.jsx:121) already honor holdStart, so the tunnel covers the load and clears onto a drawing galaxy. (2) Don't navigate on a timer that starts at the click. Pass onPeak through Lightspeed (App.jsx:116-120) via the tp:hyperspace event detail, or have go() wait for the overlay to report darkAt ≥ 1, with the 1250 ms timer kept only as a fallback. This covers the late-start case where the swap showed through a 79%-dark overlay. (3) clampStart(start, lastNow, now, maxStep = 50) in timeline.js, used in both overlay loops, so a starved overlay pauses instead of skipping its tunnel. Caveat: the jump sound runs on wall time (Hyperspace.jsx:73-77), so the boom can drift off the flash, and the intro jump gets longer under load. (4) Prefetch import('../pages/Galaxy') and import('../components/galaxy/module') when Star Wars is selected or go() starts, the way travel.js:44 prefetches the surface. (5) `.page-enter:has(.universe-page) { animation: none; }` in index.css, so a world page never fades in over the light body.
proposals.tests: timeline.test.js: clampStart leaves 16 ms steps alone and absorbs a 2 s gap down to 50 ms. A pending hold keeps holdStart at HOLD_AT until released, and is released by its timeout. Releasing twice is harmless. Browser check on a production build (vite build --outDir <scratch>; vite preview), light mode, with the prodentry.mjs timeline: the overlay canvas is removed only after the galaxy's data-gl='on'; the galaxy page commits only while the overlay is fully dark; no sampled state with the galaxy page under opacity 1 and no overlay.

proposals.title: One owner of the pixel ratio (galaxy 1.5 cap from the first frame), with an explicit call on DPR 1
proposals.description: gfx.js keeps size and ratio. setSize(w,h) and setRatio(r) both call apply(): renderer.setPixelRatio(fit(size.w, size.h, ratio)) then renderer.setSize(size.w, size.h, false). makeGfx takes an optional fit. In webgl.js remove the setSize override (58-62) and pass fit: (w,h,r) => fitRatio(w,h,r,{ side: maxSide(renderer) }), both exported from lib/three/renderer. Leave createRenderer's fit and watchdog alone: useScene pages rely on them, and the runtime never calls gl.watch. Caveats: (a) This changes every runtime world on screens under DPR 1.25. Earth, Mario64, Minecraft and the surface draw at 1.25 today after place() and would draw at 1.0, as quality.js's header intends and quality.test.js:29-37 pins. Check those worlds visually, or deliberately keep minRatio. (b) Skipping when the buffer is unchanged means place() no longer clears a re-attached canvas, which shows its old frame until drawn (reattach.mjs). Ship proposal 6 (fade while loading) with it. (c) post.js:217 then picks samples at the ratio actually drawn.
proposals.tests: New gfx.test.js with a fake renderer: setRatio(1.5) then setSize(320,180) → pixel ratio 1.5, buffer 480x270. The same setSize again → no renderer calls. setRatio(1.275) → 408x229. A fit capping at side 4096 is honored. Browser check (ratio2.mjs) at DPR 2: renderer ratio equals gfx.ratio = 1.5 after load and after a window resize.

proposals.title: Governor warm-up per world, a real reset, and a floor that needs late frames
proposals.description: (a) Add a full reset to pace.js: level 0, hold = wait, changedAt/upAt = -Infinity, stuck 0, recent cleared. Today reset() (48-53) keeps the level, so quality.reset() followed by the next step jumps 0→4 (resetsim.mjs). quality.reset uses it. pace.reset's only caller is quality.js:73; the universe, Rick and Morty and Cybertron scenes use their own paces. (b) Call quality.reset() and a new quality.hold(3000) (ignore frames until the first frame + 3 s) at the start of build(), before `gfx.setRatio(ratioFor(module))` (runtime.js:197), not in begin(). Otherwise the renderer keeps the old scaled ratio while quality reports level 0. (c) Floor only when the pace reports it is stuck at its softest with frames still late: expose pace.stuck (pace.js:92-97), replacing the plain 2.5 s timer at quality.js:61-69. Make the 'floors once' test's fake pace report stuck.
proposals.tests: pace.test.js: after hard reset, level 0 and the next late run steps to 1, not +1 from the old level. quality.test.js: late frames within hold(3000) never change the level; the same frames after it do. Sitting at the last level but not stuck never floors; once stuck it floors once. runtime.test.js: a mount resets quality before setRatio, so setRatio gets the scale-1 ratio. pace-sim2 trace E as a table test: 0 changes in the first 3 s.

proposals.title: Soften the galaxy through its post composer instead of resizing the canvas
proposals.description: Do what the universe map does (universe/scene.js:4321-4330: pace → post.sharpness, canvas size unchanged). Add a module option (fromScene(..., { ratio: 1.5, soften: 'post' }), runtime/module.js:233-239). Under it, runtime.js frame() keeps gfx at the unscaled ratioUnder(cap) (a new quality.ratioUnder(cap, { unscaled: true }) or min(cap, budget.ratio, dpr)) and still calls world.lowerQuality(level). In galaxy scene.js lowerQuality (2230-2236) set post.sharpness = STEPS[Math.min(level, STEPS.length - 1)]. post.render then draws the passes at renderer ratio × sharp over a canvas that keeps its size (post.js:275-299), so the HUD stays crisp and nothing is resized. The scene's planet detail already follows post.sharpness (scene.js:1761; bodies.setDetail is a uniform, bodies.js:389-391). Stars stay sized by gfx.ratio, which no longer changes. Proposals 1 and 3 still matter for the other worlds and for window resizes.
proposals.tests: runtime.test.js: a soften:'post' module with quality.frame → 2 → gfx.setRatio not called with a scaled ratio, world.lowerQuality(2) called. post.test.js (or scene-level): sharpness 0.72 changes the composer's pixel ratio on the next render() but not renderer.getPixelRatio().

proposals.title: Fade the world canvas in on its first frame
proposals.description: runtime.css: `.world-host[data-gl='loading'] > .world-canvas { opacity: 0; } .world-canvas { transition: opacity 0.4s var(--ease-out); }`, matching .scene-canvas (index.css:904-905). This turns the pop-in into a fade and also hides a stale re-attached frame (needed with proposal 3). Caveats: Earth's own rules (earth.css:25-26) out-rank the transition and are unaffected. After a handover's begin(), status is 'ready' for one or two frames before 'on' (runtime.js:238, 104), so data-gl goes to 'loading' briefly under the snapshot cover, a small dip. It is safer to scope the rule to fresh mounts, for example a data-fresh attribute set by the runtime in mount() and cleared on 'on'.
proposals.tests: No Vitest (CSS). Browser check: brightness across the first galaxy draw rises over ~0.4 s. scripts/galaxy-check.mjs still passes. A land → surface → take-off round trip shows no brightness dip under the cover.

proposals.title: Never present a resized buffer undrawn: apply host resizes at the start of the next frame
proposals.description: Prefer deferring over drawing inside rt.resize. resize(w,h) (runtime.js:271-276) stores pending = {w,h} and kicks the loop. frame() applies it before the draw: gfx.setSize, then world.resize. The browser shows the old buffer stretched for one frame instead of a blank one, and no world is drawn from a ResizeObserver callback or from adopt()'s layout effect, which would emit scene events during React's commit. Skip when the rounded size is unchanged, since the RO's first callback repeats the size. If drawing in resize() is chosen instead, guard it on the loop's can() (shown && visible()) and on a real buffer change. Not an entry fix (no resize happens on entry), but it removes the blink while resizing a window.
proposals.tests: runtime.test.js: mount; rt.resize(800,450) → gfx.setSize not yet called. On the next tick, setSize(800,450) and world.resize(800,450) come before world.draw. rt.resize to the current size → no setSize. With no current world, nothing.

proposals.title: Share one pending backend between concurrent mounts
proposals.description: backendFor (runtime.js:180-191): keep `pending = { kind, promise: makeBackend(...) }` and await it, so a second mount while the first is creating reuses it. Assign gfx once, when it resolves. This removes the dev context leak and the race where the surviving backend never got build's setRatio (gfx.ratio 1, drawing at 2.0, post samples 0).
proposals.tests: runtime.test.js: makeBackend returns a deferred promise; two rt.mount calls before resolving; resolve; flush → makeBackend called once, rt.gfx is that backend, and its setRatio got ratioFor(module). Also resolve two deferreds in reverse order (if a kind change forces two) → the gfx used by the winning build is rt.gfx.

proposals.title: (Not flicker; found while verifying) Don't carry `shown` into the next world
proposals.description: rt keeps `shown` (runtime.js:61) across unmount and mount, and begin() hands it to the new world (236). useWorld's IntersectionObserver ignores its first callback while the module is still loading (useWorld.js:75-80). So after a world whose box was scrolled out of view (setVisible(false)), the galaxy's loop never runs: loop can() is false (runtime.js:128), status stays 'ready' and 'Plotting a course…' never goes. Set shown = true in mount() and handover(), or let useWorld apply the IO state when rt.loading === module.
proposals.tests: runtime.test.js: mount A; rt.setVisible(false); unmount; mount B → the first tick draws and status becomes 'on' (rtsim.mjs reproduces the stuck case today).

constraints: Read-only investigation: no tracked file was edited. The production build went to the scratchpad (vite build --outDir <scratch>/skeptic/dist). git status is clean.
createRenderer's private pixelRatio, fit() and watchdog (lib/three/renderer.js:36-101) serve useScene pages; change the runtime's path only (gfx.js/webgl.js).
The snapshot cover must be taken in the same task as the draw (runtime.js:152-167, gfx.js:40-41). Keep the snapshot after world.draw when reordering frame().

Tests that pin behaviour: runtime.test.js 'a new quality level sets the ratio and tells the world' and the module-cap test (317-337); 'a mount during loading wins' (90-109, uses a synchronous makeBackend, so it does not exercise the race); the held-cover/adopt tests (360-407); quality.test.js:29-37 pins ratio 1 at dpr 1 for tier high (keeping the 1.25 minRatio would break it); quality.test.js:53-74 floor test.
pace.reset() has one caller (quality.js:73). The universe, Rick and Morty and Cybertron scenes each make their own createPace and never reset it, so a real level reset is safe there.
The galaxy's 1.5 cap is intended (galaxy/module.js:3-4, 'at 1.5x at most as it always has'). quality.js's header intends a 1x screen to draw at 1, though the runtime draws at 1.25 today.

holdJump/holdStart are already honored by Hyperspace2D (Hyperspace.jsx:185), the 3D overlay (hyperspace3d/scene.js:310) and the crews' JumpCanvas (jumps/JumpCanvas.jsx:121). A cross-page hold must be released on every outcome: 'on', 'failed', 'lost', 3D off or WorldGate held (meant false), GalaxyView unmount, and its timeout.
No preserveDrawingBuffer: frames are read in their own task. DEV's window.__tpKeepFrames is the only exception (renderer.js:39).

Dev exaggerates: StrictMode double mount (main.jsx), checkShaderErrors (renderer.js:44), unbundled module loading. Verify the hand-off fixes in a production build; headless SwiftShader also stretches main-thread stalls to seconds.
The universe map softens through post.sharpness without resizing the canvas (universe/scene.js:4321-4330). The galaxy's post supports the same (post.js:270-299).

The pace ignores gaps over 250 ms (pace.js:68), so headless runs never exercise the governor; feed it traces in Node instead (pace-sim2.mjs pattern, with an extension-resolving loader such as skeptic/reg.mjs).
openQuestions: Which flicker does the user see? (a) The hand-off: overlay cut or cleared onto the loading page, white wash in light mode, scene popping in. (b) A one-frame blink with a sharpness and star-size change a second or a few after arrival (governor steps; most likely on a DPR-2 laptop with a mid GPU, given the 2.0-with-4x-MSAA draw). (c) Something else, such as point-star shimmer: stars are 1-5 px sprites with a smoothstep disc (sky.js:186-196) and may twinkle while the arrival's FOV eases. Light or dark mode, the screen's DPR, and dev or the deployed site would separate these.
How often the governor steps on entry on real hardware is unmeasured. A dev-only console line from quality.on() (level, scale, gfx.ratio, renderer ratio) on the user's machine would settle it.

Should runtime worlds on 1x screens keep the 1.25 supersample they get today through fit(), or drop to 1.0 as quality.js documents? This decides proposal 3's visual impact on Earth, Mario64, Minecraft and the surface.

The 2.2 s main-thread task right after the click in the production headless run, before the overlay's first frame, is unprofiled. It is probably WebGL context and three renderer creation for the overlay in SwiftShader, short on a real GPU. If it is long on real devices, proposal 2's 'navigate on the overlay's dark' becomes more important.
Latent, not flicker: WorldGate re-checks storage after mount (WorldGate.jsx:54-56), and free < 32 MB flips `held`, unmounting the galaxy mid-load. This is rare on desktops and was not tested.
